question: The Pandya Kingdom was first mentioned by Megasthenes, who said that their kingdom was famous for pearls.Their capital was:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madurai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pandya Kingdom was one of the three ancient Tamil dynasties (Sangam Age), along with the Cheras and Cholas, and had Madurai as its capital. (पांड्य साम्राज्य — मदुरई राजधानी)

 

• The Greek ambassador Megasthenes, who visited the court of Chandragupta Maurya, mentioned the Pandya kingdom in his account 'Indica', describing it as ruled by a queen and famous for its pearl fisheries.

 

• Madurai, situated on the banks of the Vaigai river, was also a great centre of Tamil learning and hosted the Tamil Sangams (Sangam literary assemblies).

 

• The Pandyas controlled the pearl fisheries of the Gulf of Mannar, which made their kingdom famous for pearls in ancient Greek and Roman accounts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pandya emblem was the fish (carp), and their kingdom is also mentioned in the Mahabharata and by the Roman writer Pliny the Elder.

 

• The Pandyas had trade relations with the Roman Empire, exporting pearls, spices and muslin.

 

NOTE

 

• Thanjavur (Option 1): It was the capital of the medieval Chola dynasty under rulers like Rajaraja Chola I.

 

• Uraiyur (Option 2): It was the ancient capital of the early Cholas, famous for cotton trade.

 

• Kaveripatnam (Option 4): Also known as Puhar, it was a major port city and secondary capital of the Cholas.

question: Harivarasanam award is given in the field of music by which of the following state governments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Harivarasanam Award is conferred annually by the Government of Kerala to honour outstanding contributions in the field of music. (हरिवरासनम पुरस्कार — केरल सरकार)

 

• The award is named after the devotional hymn 'Harivarasanam', traditionally sung at the Sabarimala Temple in Kerala while closing the sanctum sanctorum for the night.

 

• It is presented by the Kerala state government as part of its cultural and devotional music promotion initiatives, and carries a citation, cash prize and memento.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sabarimala Temple, dedicated to Lord Ayyappa, is located in the Periyar Tiger Reserve in Pathanamthitta district, Kerala.

 

• Kerala also confers other cultural honours such as the Swathi Sangeetha Puraskaram for Carnatic music.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka, Maharashtra and Himachal Pradesh (Options 2, 3 and 4): These state governments confer their own respective cultural and music awards, but none of them administers the Harivarasanam Award, which is specific to Kerala.

question: Easter festival is celebrated by which community?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Christian.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Easter is one of the most important festivals of the Christian community, celebrating the resurrection of Jesus Christ three days after his crucifixion. (ईस्टर — ईसाई समुदाय)

 

• It is observed in the spring season, typically on a Sunday between late March and late April, and marks the culmination of Holy Week, which begins with Palm Sunday and includes Good Friday.

 

• Common Easter traditions include church services, fasting during Lent (the 40 days preceding Easter), and symbols such as Easter eggs and the Easter Bunny, representing new life and rebirth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Christmas, celebrating the birth of Jesus Christ on 25 December, is another major Christian festival.

 

• Good Friday, observed on the Friday before Easter, commemorates the crucifixion of Jesus Christ.

 

NOTE

 

• Parsi (Option 2): Their major festivals include Navroz (Parsi New Year) and Pateti.

 

• Hindu (Option 3): Major Hindu festivals include Diwali, Holi and Dussehra.

 

• Sikh (Option 4): Major Sikh festivals include Baisakhi and Gurpurab.

question: Which of the following Sikh reform movements was started in 1873 in Amritsar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Singh Sabha Movement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Singh Sabha Movement was started in 1873 at Amritsar with the founding of the Sri Guru Singh Sabha, in response to the activities of Christian missionaries, the Arya Samaj and Brahmo Samaj among the Sikhs. (सिंह सभा आंदोलन — अमृतसर, 1873)

 

• Its main objectives were to reform Sikhism, restore the pristine glory of Sikh teachings, propagate Gurmukhi and Punjabi language and literature, and counter conversions out of Sikhism.

 

• Prominent leaders associated with the movement included Thakur Singh Sandhawalia and Baba Khem Singh Bedi, and it later split into the Amritsar Singh Sabha (moderate) and the Lahore Singh Sabha (more reformist, led by figures like Gurmukh Singh).

 

• The movement laid the intellectual and organisational foundation for later Sikh reform bodies such as the Chief Khalsa Diwan (1902).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Singh Sabha Movement eventually led to the Gurdwara Reform Movement in the early 20th century, aimed at freeing gurdwaras from corrupt Mahants.

 

• The Chief Khalsa Diwan, formed in 1902, unified various Singh Sabhas into a single central body.

 

NOTE

 

• Babbar Akali Movement (Option 1): A militant offshoot of the Akali Movement in the 1920s that used revolutionary methods against corrupt gurdwara management and British rule.

 

• Akali Movement (Option 2): A movement in the early 1920s aimed at freeing gurdwaras from the control of corrupt Mahants and placing them under the SGPC.

 

• Gurudwara Movement (Option 4): A broader early-20th-century movement (1920-1925) that culminated in the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925, and is often used interchangeably with the Akali Movement, but it was not started in 1873.

question: ‘Bhagirathi’ and ‘Alaknanda’ rivers confluence at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Devaprayag.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Devaprayag, located in Uttarakhand, is the site where the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers meet to form the Ganga (Ganges) river. (देवप्रयाग — भागीरथी व अलकनंदा का संगम)

 

• Devaprayag is the last of the Panch Prayag (five sacred river confluences) in the Garhwal Himalayas and is considered the point of origin of the river Ganga in its own name.

 

• From Devaprayag onwards, the combined river is known as the Ganga, which flows onward towards Rishikesh and Haridwar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Panch Prayag in sequence are: Vishnuprayag (Alaknanda + Dhauliganga), Nandprayag (Alaknanda + Nandakini), Karnaprayag (Alaknanda + Pindar), Rudraprayag (Alaknanda + Mandakini), and Devaprayag (Alaknanda + Bhagirathi).

 

• The Bhagirathi river originates from the Gangotri Glacier (Gaumukh).

 

NOTE

 

• Joshimath (Option 1): A town near Vishnuprayag, an important gateway to Badrinath and Auli, but not a river confluence of Bhagirathi and Alaknanda.

 

• Haridwar (Option 2): The Ganga enters the plains here; it is downstream of the Bhagirathi-Alaknanda confluence, not the confluence point itself.

 

• Karanprayag (Option 3): This is the confluence of the Alaknanda and Pindar rivers, not Bhagirathi.

question: Which of the following institutions has contributed mainly in improving the economic status of the poor women in rural areas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Self-help Group.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Self-Help Group (SHG) is a small, voluntary association of people, typically 10-20 poor women from similar socio-economic backgrounds, who pool small savings and provide each other mutual credit support. (स्वयं सहायता समूह — ग्रामीण महिलाओं का आर्थिक सशक्तिकरण)

 

• SHGs have played a major role in microfinance and rural women's economic empowerment in India by promoting savings habits, easy access to credit without collateral, and small-scale income-generating activities.

 

• The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, launched by NABARD in 1992, is the world's largest microfinance programme and has been central to improving the economic status of poor rural women.

 

• The Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) promotes SHGs as its core institutional platform for rural poverty alleviation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) was established in 1982 and pioneered the SHG-Bank Linkage model in India.

 

• The DAY-NRLM, launched in 2011, aims to organise rural poor women into SHGs and federate them into higher-level institutions.

 

NOTE

 

• Indira Awas Yojana (Option 1): A rural housing scheme aimed at providing houses to the rural poor, not specifically targeted at women's economic empowerment.

 

• Integrated Development Project (Option 2): A generic rural development programme, not specifically focused on the economic status of poor women.

 

• Rural Health Scheme (Option 4): Focuses on healthcare delivery in rural areas, not on economic empowerment.

question: Identify a spiral-shaped bacteria.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Spirillum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bacteria are classified on the basis of their shape, and Spirillum refers to bacteria that are rigid, spiral or corkscrew-shaped. (स्पिरिलम — सर्पिल आकार के जीवाणु)

 

• Spirillum bacteria move using external flagella and are typically found in stagnant water; an example is Spirillum volutans.

 

• Bacterial shapes are broadly classified into four types: Coccus (spherical), Bacillus (rod-shaped), Spirillum (spiral/helical), and Vibrio (comma-shaped/curved rod).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Spirochaetes are another group of flexible, coiled bacteria (e.g., the causative agent of syphilis and leptospirosis), distinct from rigid Spirilla.

 

• Bacterial shape influences motility, nutrient uptake and the way bacteria colonise different environments.

 

NOTE

 

• Bacillus (Option 1): Refers to rod-shaped bacteria, e.g. *Lactobacillus*, *Bacillus anthracis*.

 

• Coccus (Option 3): Refers to spherical/round-shaped bacteria, e.g. *Streptococcus*, *Staphylococcus*.

 

• Vibrio (Option 4): Refers to comma-shaped/curved rod bacteria, e.g. *Vibrio cholerae*, which causes cholera — this is curved, not fully spiral.

question: In which year did the Central Government launch the National Air Sports Policy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2022.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Air Sports Policy (NASP) 2022 was launched by the Ministry of Civil Aviation in July 2022, with the objective of making India one of the top air sports nations by 2030. (राष्ट्रीय एयर स्पोर्ट्स नीति — 2022)

 

• It was released by Union Minister of Civil Aviation Jyotiraditya Scindia, and covers air sports such as aeromodelling, ballooning, drones, gliding, powered aircraft, skydiving and paragliding.

 

• The policy aims to establish the Air Sports Federation of India (ASFI) as a self-regulatory body to oversee and promote air sports activities in the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The NASP 2022 aims to make India a top-5 air sports nation in the world by 2030.

 

• It also seeks to enhance safety standards, insurance coverage, and promote air sports tourism across India.

 

NOTE

 

• 2021, 2023 and 2020 (Options 2, 3 and 4): These years are incorrect; the National Air Sports Policy was formally released in 2022.

question: As of 14 October 2021, which Indian footballer was in the news for breaking Pele's 77 international goals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sunil Chhetri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sunil Chhetri, captain of the Indian national football team, is one of the highest active international goal scorers in the world, ranking behind only Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi for a period. (सुनील छेत्री — भारतीय फुटबॉल कप्तान)

 

• As of 14 October 2021, Chhetri's international goal tally had gone past the widely cited figure of Pele's 77 international goals, making headlines in Indian sports media.

 

• Chhetri had earlier, in June 2021, surpassed Lionel Messi's international goal tally as well, becoming one of the top active international goal-scorers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sunil Chhetri made his international debut in 2005 and has led India in multiple SAFF Championship and Intercontinental Cup title wins.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2019 and the Khel Ratna Award in 2021.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhaichung Bhutia (Option 1): A former Indian football captain and one of India's football pioneers, but he retired before this record was set.

 

• Gurpreet Singh Sandhu (Option 3): The current Indian national team goalkeeper, not a goal-scoring record holder.

 

• Sandesh Jhingan (Option 4): A defender for the Indian national football team, not associated with this goal-scoring record.

question: Which of the following Acts introduced ‘provincial autonomy’ by discontinuing the application of dyarchy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government of India Act, 1935.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of India Act, 1935 introduced 'provincial autonomy', abolishing the system of dyarchy in the provinces that had been introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919. (भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1935 — प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता)

 

• Under provincial autonomy, provinces were given separate legal identities, and elected provincial ministries responsible to provincial legislatures were made to administer all subjects in the provincial list, ending the earlier division of subjects into 'reserved' and 'transferred' categories.

 

• The Act also introduced dyarchy at the Centre (a system it had removed from the provinces) and provided for an All India Federation, though the federal part never came into force.

 

• Provincial autonomy came into effect in 1937, following provincial elections held under the Act.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Government of India Act, 1935 also provided for a Federal Court (established in 1937) and separate communal electorates.

 

• It served as the basis for much of the structure of the Constitution of India, 1950.

 

NOTE

 

• Government of India Act, 1919 (Option 1): Introduced dyarchy in the provinces, i.e. the very system that the 1935 Act discontinued.

 

• Charter Act of 1813 (Option 2): Ended the East India Company's trade monopoly (except in tea and trade with China) and allowed Christian missionaries into India.

 

• India Council Act, 1909 (Option 3): Also called the Morley-Minto Reforms, it introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

question: Which committee recommended Constitutional recognition for the local government bodies in 1989?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PK Thungon Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The P.K. Thungon Committee, constituted in 1988, submitted its report in 1989, strongly recommending Constitutional recognition and status for local self-government bodies (both Panchayats and Municipalities). (पी.के. थुंगन समिति — स्थानीय निकायों को संवैधानिक दर्जा)

 

• Its recommendations paved the way for the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (Panchayati Raj Institutions) and the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (Urban Local Bodies), which came into force in 1993.

 

• The Committee suggested a three-tier Panchayati Raj structure and regular elections to local bodies, with constitutional backing to prevent arbitrary dissolution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 73rd Amendment added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution for Panchayats.

 

• The 74th Amendment added Part IX-A and the Twelfth Schedule for Municipalities.

 

NOTE

 

• Ashok Mehta Committee (Option 1): Constituted in 1977, it recommended a two-tier Panchayati Raj system.

 

• Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (Option 3): Constituted in 1957, it recommended the original three-tier Panchayati Raj system for democratic decentralisation.

 

• Verma Committee (Option 4): Related to disinvestment and financial restructuring of PSUs, not local government bodies.

question: Which of the following is NOT related to reticulate venation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maize.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Venation refers to the arrangement of veins in leaves. Reticulate (net-like) venation is characteristic of dicotyledonous plants, while parallel venation is characteristic of monocotyledonous plants. (शिरा विन्यास — मक्का में समानांतर शिरा विन्यास)

 

• Maize is a monocotyledonous plant and hence exhibits parallel venation, not reticulate venation.

 

• China rose, Tulsi and Coriander are all dicotyledonous plants and show typical reticulate (net-like) venation in their leaves.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of parallel venation (monocots) include wheat, rice, sugarcane, banana and grasses.

 

• Other examples of reticulate venation (dicots) include mango, peepal, rose and mustard.

 

NOTE

 

• China rose (Option 1): A dicot ornamental plant (*Hibiscus rosa-sinensis*), showing reticulate venation.

 

• Tulsi (Option 2): A dicot medicinal herb (*Ocimum sanctum*), showing reticulate venation.

 

• Coriander (Option 4): A dicot herb (*Coriandrum sativum*), showing reticulate venation.

question: In which of the following Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka is the Kalinga war mentioned?
solution_text:
The correct answer is XIII.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Major Rock Edict XIII of Emperor Ashoka is the most important edict describing the Kalinga War and its aftermath. (अशोक का तेरहवाँ शिलालेख — कलिंग युद्ध)

 

• In this edict, Ashoka expresses deep remorse over the massive bloodshed and suffering caused by the Kalinga War, stating that 'one hundred and fifty thousand were deported, one hundred thousand were killed, and many more died'.

 

• The edict also describes Ashoka's subsequent embrace of Dhamma (Buddhist principles of righteousness) and his resolve to conquer through Dhamma-Vijaya (moral conquest) rather than military conquest.

 

• This edict is notably absent from the Kalinga region itself (found instead at Dhauli and Jaugada with modified versions), likely to avoid demoralising the local population.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kalinga War was fought around 261 BCE, and its aftermath led to Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism.

 

• Major Rock Edict XII deals with religious tolerance, and Major Rock Edict XI deals with the concept and gifts of Dhamma.

 

NOTE

 

• XII (Option 1): Deals with tolerance towards all religious sects and their followers.

 

• X (Option 2): Deals with Ashoka's rejection of fame and glory, emphasising Dhamma instead.

 

• XI (Option 4): Describes the gift of Dhamma as the greatest of all gifts.

question: Who among the following is NOT a member of the National Human Rights Commission?
option_2: Former Chief Justice of the High Court
option_3: Former Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
option_4: Former Judge of the Supreme Court
solution_text:
The correct answer is District Magistrate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India was established in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, and a District Magistrate is not a statutory member of the Commission. (राष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार आयोग — गठन)

 

• As per the Act (amended in 2019), the NHRC consists of a Chairperson (who has been a Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court) and Members, which include a former Chief Justice of the Supreme Court or a Judge of the Supreme Court, and a former Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court, along with other members having knowledge of human rights.

 

• It also has certain ex-officio members, namely the Chairpersons of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Women, Minorities, Backward Classes, Child Rights, and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities.

 

• A District Magistrate is a district-level executive officer and has no statutory role in the composition of the NHRC.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The NHRC is headquartered in New Delhi and functions as a statutory (not constitutional) body.

 

• Each state also has its own State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) under the same Act.

 

NOTE

 

• Former Chief Justice of the High Court (Option 2): Eligible to be appointed as a Member of the NHRC.

 

• Former Chief Justice of the Supreme Court (Option 3): Eligible to be appointed as Chairperson or Member of the NHRC.

 

• Former Judge of the Supreme Court (Option 4): Eligible to be appointed as a Member of the NHRC.

question: Which of the following is an inosilicate amphibole mineral used in highway construction and as railroad ballast?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hornblende.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hornblende is a common rock-forming inosilicate mineral of the amphibole group, typically dark green to black in colour, and is widely used as crushed stone for highway construction and railroad ballast. (हॉर्नब्लेंड — एम्फिबोल खनिज)

 

• It is a complex calcium, magnesium, iron and aluminium silicate, commonly found in igneous and metamorphic rocks such as granite, diorite, gneiss and schist.

 

• Due to its hardness and durability, crushed hornblende-bearing rock is widely used as an aggregate in road-building and as railway track ballast.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Inosilicates (chain silicates) include two mineral groups: pyroxenes (single-chain) and amphiboles (double-chain, e.g., hornblende, actinolite, tremolite).

 

• Asbestos is another well-known amphibole-group mineral, historically used for its heat-resistant fibrous form.

 

NOTE

 

• Shale (Option 1): A fine-grained sedimentary rock, not a mineral, formed from compacted mud/clay.

 

• Olivine (Option 2): A nesosilicate (island silicate) mineral, not an inosilicate amphibole.

 

• Geyserite (Option 3): A form of opaline silica deposited around geysers and hot springs, not an amphibole mineral.

question: Ranjana Prakash Desai who became the first woman chairperson of the Press Council of India originally worked in which of the following organs of the government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Judiciary.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai is a former Judge of the Supreme Court of India and became the first woman Chairperson of the Press Council of India (PCI), taking charge in 2020. (रंजना प्रकाश देसाई — प्रेस परिषद की पहली महिला अध्यक्ष)

 

• She served as a judge of the Bombay High Court before being elevated to the Supreme Court of India in 2011, retiring in 2014.

 

• Since she was a career judge, her original organ of government was the Judiciary.

 

• As PCI Chairperson, she oversees matters relating to press freedom and maintaining standards of newspapers and news agencies in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Press Council of India (PCI) is a statutory, quasi-judicial body established under the Press Council Act, 1978, to preserve press freedom and maintain journalistic standards.

 

• Justice Desai also headed the Justice Verma Committee's subsequent inquiry panels and other judicial commissions after her retirement.

 

NOTE

 

• Legislature, Vigilance and Executive (Options 1, 3 and 4): Justice Desai's career was in the judiciary as a High Court and Supreme Court judge, not in these organs/bodies.

question: Which state of India has the maximum number of large dams?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the National Register of Large Dams (NRLD), maintained by the Central Water Commission (CWC), Maharashtra has the highest number of large dams among all Indian states. (महाराष्ट्र — सर्वाधिक बड़े बांध)

 

• Maharashtra accounts for a substantial share (roughly one-third to two-fifths) of the total large dams in India, owing to its numerous west-flowing rivers from the Western Ghats and extensive irrigation infrastructure.

 

• Notable large dams in Maharashtra include the Koyna Dam, Jayakwadi Dam and Ujani Dam.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A 'large dam' as per CWC/ICOLD criteria is generally one with a height of 15 metres or more from the lowest foundation, or between 10-15 metres with certain additional specifications.

 

• India has the third-highest number of large dams in the world, after the USA and China.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 2): Has a significant number of large dams but ranks below Maharashtra.

 

• Odisha (Option 3): Has a comparatively smaller number of large dams than Maharashtra.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 4): Has a comparatively smaller number of large dams than Maharashtra.

question: Identify a monoatomic molecule.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Helium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A monoatomic molecule consists of a single atom and is characteristic of noble gases. Helium (He) exists in nature as single, isolated atoms and is a classic example of a monoatomic molecule. (हीलियम — एकपरमाण्विक अणु)

 

• Noble gases (Group 18 elements — Helium, Neon, Argon, Krypton, Xenon, Radon) are chemically inert due to their complete outer electron shells, so they do not bond with other atoms and exist as single atoms.

 

• Molecules made of a single type of atom bonded together (like O2, Cl2) are called diatomic, and those with more than two atoms are polyatomic.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Examples of diatomic molecules include O2, N2, H2, Cl2 and CO (carbon monoxide, a heteroatomic diatomic molecule).

 

• Examples of polyatomic molecules include O3 (ozone), CO2, H2O, NH3.

 

NOTE

 

• Carbon monoxide (Option 1): A diatomic molecule (one carbon and one oxygen atom), not monoatomic.

 

• Oxygen (Option 2): Naturally exists as O2, a diatomic molecule.

 

• Chlorine (Option 4): Naturally exists as Cl2, a diatomic molecule.

question: According to Census 2011, which district displays the highest population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thane.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India, 2011, Thane district in Maharashtra had the highest population among all districts in India, with a population of approximately 1.1 crore (11 million). (ठाणे जिला — सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या, जनगणना 2011)

 

• Thane's high population is largely attributable to its proximity to Mumbai and rapid urbanisation, including towns like Kalyan, Bhiwandi, Ulhasnagar and Mira-Bhayandar, which fell within undivided Thane district at the time of the 2011 Census.

 

• The district was later bifurcated in 2014 to create the separate Palghar district, after the Census 2011 enumeration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The second-most populous district as per Census 2011 was North Twenty Four Parganas in West Bengal.

 

• Lakshadweep, being a small Union Territory, and other small Himalayan districts recorded among the lowest district-level populations as per Census 2011.

 

NOTE

 

• Kollam (Option 1): A district in Kerala, with a much smaller population than Thane.

 

• Ajmer (Option 2): A district in Rajasthan, with a much smaller population than Thane.

 

• Pune (Option 4): A populous Maharashtra district but ranked below Thane as per Census 2011.

question:
Consider the following statements and identify the INCORRECT statement(s).

1. The ‘Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0’ scheme has been implemented under the National Food Security Act, 2003.

2. It is an ongoing, Central Government-sponsored scheme under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

3. It is extended to children aged below 6 years only.

4. Six services are provided under this scheme through the National Health Mission and Public Health Infrastructure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1, 3 and 4.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0' (also called Mission Poshan 2.0) is the umbrella scheme for Anganwadi Services, Poshan Abhiyaan, the Scheme for Adolescent Girls and the National Creche Scheme. (सक्षम आंगनवाड़ी और पोषण 2.0 — महिला एवं बाल विकास मंत्रालय)

 

• Statement 1 is incorrect: The scheme is implemented under the National Food Security Act, 2013 (not 2003), which mandates supplementary nutrition under the Anganwadi Services scheme as a legal entitlement.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: It is indeed an ongoing, Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: It is not restricted to children below 6 years only — it also covers pregnant women, lactating mothers, and adolescent girls (14-18 years), especially in Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern Region.

 

• Statement 4 is incorrect: The six services under Anganwadi Services (supplementary nutrition, pre-school non-formal education, nutrition and health education, immunisation, health check-up, and referral services) are delivered mainly through Anganwadi Centres, not specifically 'through the National Health Mission and Public Health Infrastructure'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 was launched by merging the erstwhile Anganwadi Services, Poshan Abhiyaan, Scheme for Adolescent Girls, and National Creche Scheme for FY 2021-22 to 2025-26.

 

• It aims to upgrade regular Anganwadi Centres into 'Saksham Anganwadis' with better infrastructure, clean drinking water, toilets, and electricity.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 4 (Option 2): Incorrect, since statements 1 and 3 are also factually wrong, not just statement 4.

 

• Only 1, 2 and 3 (Option 3): Incorrect, since statement 2 is actually correct, and statement 4 is also incorrect but omitted here.

 

• Only 2 and 3 (Option 4): Incorrect, since statement 2 is correct (not incorrect), and statements 1 and 4 are also incorrect but omitted here.

question: In which five-year plan was the 'food, work, and productivity' slogan used?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seventh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-1990) adopted the slogan 'food, work and productivity', focusing on increasing food-grain production, generating employment opportunities, and raising overall productivity. (सातवीं पंचवर्षीय योजना — खाद्य, कार्य और उत्पादकता)

 

• The plan gave priority to modernisation of agriculture, raising labour productivity in industry, and moving towards self-sufficiency in food-grain production.

 

• It was formulated under the Rajiv Gandhi government, with Manmohan Singh as Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission for part of its tenure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-85) focused on direct attack on poverty through programmes like IRDP.

 

• The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-79) carried the slogan 'Garibi Hatao' (Remove Poverty).

 

NOTE

 

• Sixth (Option 1): Its focus was on poverty alleviation and employment generation through IRDP and NREP, not this specific slogan.

 

• Fifth (Option 2): Its slogan was 'Garibi Hatao', not 'food, work and productivity'.

 

• Fourth (Option 3): Its focus was 'growth with stability' and self-reliance, not this slogan.

question: Which of the following chemical reactions takes place when quick lime reacts with water?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CaO(s) + H2O(l) → Ca(OH)2(aq).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Quick lime (Calcium oxide, CaO) reacts vigorously with water in a highly exothermic reaction to form Slaked lime (Calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2). (बुझा हुआ चूना — CaO + H2O से Ca(OH)2)

 

• The correct balanced chemical equation is: CaO(s) + H2O(l) → Ca(OH)2(aq), and this process is called the 'slaking of lime'.

 

• This reaction releases a large amount of heat and is used commercially in whitewashing, the manufacture of bleaching powder, and in the building/construction industry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Calcium hydroxide (slaked lime) is also known as 'chuna' and is used in the preparation of bleaching powder (CaOCl2) by reacting with chlorine gas.

 

• Quicklime (CaO) is obtained industrially by heating limestone (CaCO3), a process called calcination: CaCO3 → CaO + CO2.

 

NOTE

 

• CaO(s) + H2O(l) → Ca + H2(aq) (Option 1): This is not a valid/balanced reaction; calcium oxide does not decompose water to release free calcium and hydrogen gas.

 

• C(s) + O2(g) → CO2(g) (Option 2): This represents the combustion of carbon, unrelated to the reaction of quicklime with water.

 

• CH4(g) + 2O2(g) → CO2(g) + 2H2O(g) (Option 4): This represents the combustion of methane, unrelated to the reaction of quicklime with water.

question: With which of the following dances is Yamini Krishnamurthy associated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Yamini Krishnamurthy is a renowned Indian classical dancer, most celebrated as an exponent of Bharatanatyam (she is also trained in Kuchipudi). (यामिनी कृष्णमूर्ति — भरतनाट्यम नृत्यांगना)

 

• She trained under legendary gurus including Ellappa Pillai for Bharatanatyam and Vempati Chinna Satyam for Kuchipudi.

 

• She has been honoured with the Padma Shri (1968), Padma Bhushan (2001), and Padma Vibhushan (2016) for her contribution to Indian classical dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Yamini Krishnamurthy also holds a Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and is regarded as one of the pioneers who popularised Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi on the world stage.

 

• She founded the Yamini School of Dance in New Delhi to train future generations of dancers.

 

NOTE

 

• Mohiniyattam (Option 2): A classical dance form of Kerala, not associated with Yamini Krishnamurthy.

 

• Odissi (Option 3): A classical dance form of Odisha, popularised by exponents like Kelucharan Mohapatra, not Yamini Krishnamurthy.

 

• Sattriya (Option 4): A classical dance form of Assam, originating from Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras), not associated with Yamini Krishnamurthy.

question: Who among the following is the first vocalist to receive the Bharat Ratna in 2008 and is also credited to have popularised 'Khyal Gayaki'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Bhimsen Joshi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, a legendary Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana Gharana, was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2008, becoming the first vocalist to receive India's highest civilian honour. (पंडित भीमसेन जोशी — भारत रत्न, ख्याल गायकी)

 

• He is widely credited with popularising 'Khyal Gayaki' (a major genre of Hindustani classical vocal music) among the masses through his powerful and emotive renditions.

 

• He was also famous for popular bhajans and devotional compositions such as 'Jo Bhaje Hari Ko Sada', and was honoured with the Padma Shri (1972), Padma Bhushan (1985) and Padma Vibhushan (1999) prior to the Bharat Ratna.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kirana Gharana of Hindustani classical music was founded by Ustad Abdul Karim Khan.

 

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi also co-founded the Sawai Gandharva Bhimsen Mahotsav, a major annual classical music festival in Pune.

 

NOTE

 

• Begum Akhtar (Option 2): A legendary Ghazal, Dadra and Thumri singer, honoured with the Padma Bhushan, but not a Bharat Ratna recipient.

 

• Vishnu Digambar Palushkar (Option 3): A pioneering Hindustani classical musician and founder of the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, but not a Bharat Ratna recipient.

 

• Gangubai Hangal (Option 4): A renowned Kirana Gharana vocalist, honoured with the Padma Vibhushan, but not a Bharat Ratna recipient.

question: The third edition of the Khelo India University Games was hosted by which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 3rd edition of the Khelo India University Games (KIUG) 2023 was hosted by Uttar Pradesh, held from 25 May to 3 June 2023, with venues across Lucknow, Varanasi, Gorakhpur, Noida and Delhi (shooting). (खेलो इंडिया विश्वविद्यालय खेल — तीसरा संस्करण, उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• The Games were formally declared open by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Ekana Stadium, Lucknow.

 

• Over 4,700 athletes from more than 200 universities across India participated across various sporting disciplines in this edition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 1st Khelo India University Games (2020) were held in Bhubaneswar, Odisha.

 

• The 2nd Khelo India University Games (2021, held in 2022) were hosted by Karnataka, with Bengaluru as the primary venue.

 

NOTE

 

• Haryana (Option 2): Has hosted other Khelo India events but not the 3rd KIUG.

 

• Punjab (Option 3): Has not hosted the Khelo India University Games edition in question.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 4): Hosted the Khelo India Youth Games 2022, not the 3rd University Games.
